Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Quadratic Functions

The Shape of a Jump

Three forms, one flight path

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Quadratic Graphs
Standards
HSF-IF.C.7a, HSF-IF.C.8a, HSF-IF.B.4

Students graph quadratics from standard, vertex and factored form, connect each form to the vertex, axis, intercepts and direction, and write a quadratic for a jump from its features.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Graph a quadratic from standard, vertex or factored form.
  • Identify the vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts and direction of opening.
  • Explain which features each form shows directly.
  • Write a quadratic from its features or from points.

3Essential question

Why does a jump’s flight path make a parabola, and which form of its equation tells you the most?

5MTB connection

Ignoring air resistance, a rider in the air follows a parabola. The zeros are takeoff and landing, the vertex is the peak, and the axis of symmetry is halfway between.

Each form of the equation answers a different builder’s question: factored form says where to put the landing, vertex form says how high the rider goes, standard form says the height at the lip.

The mathOn the trail
ZerosTakeoff and landing
VertexPeak height and where it happens
a < 0Gravity pulls the path down
Axis of symmetryHalfway point of the flight
